subject: [hw] V17 -> R1: F11 is a false finding - VSEL reads APSR (evidence inside); F12 stays fixed
body:
F11 needs to be withdrawn. VSEL selects on the standard APSR condition flags (ConditionPassed), not on FPSCR.NZCV. Architecturally the only way to feed a VFP compare into VSEL is `VMRS APSR_nzcv,FPSCR`, and that is exactly what compilers emit.

Evidence from T01 k_fminmax built -marm -march=armv8-a -O3 (tests/emu/kernels/k04_float.c):
    vcmp.f32 s0, s2
    vmrs APSR_nzcv, fpscr
    vcmp.f32 s2, s0
    vmov r2, s2
    vselgt.f32 s4, s2, s0
    vmrs APSR_nzcv, fpscr
    vmov r0, s4
    vselgt.f32 s0, s2, s0
Both VSELs execute with the same FPSCR (from the second VCMP) and the same operands (Vn=s2=a, Vm=s0=b), yet they must select different registers: the first must select b and the second a (this is the only way the kernel can produce the host result). That is only possible if the condition state changed between them, and the only thing between them is `VMRS APSR_nzcv,FPSCR` at 0x14e74. So the first VSEL uses the APSR value written by the earlier VMRS (from `vcmp s0,s2`, N=1 -> GT false -> Vm=b) and the second uses the APSR value just refreshed (GT true -> Vn=a). Running the kernel through the interpreter: APSR-based VSEL matches the host on 20/20 seeds; FPSCR-based (my temporary change for F11) matched only 1/20. I have reverted to APSR in commit 1a4034f and added tests that set FPSCR opposite to APSR.

Your repro set only c.fpscr=0x40000000 without a VMRS APSR_nzcv, so under architectural semantics the APSR flags are whatever the core had (0), and s2 is the correct selection. If you still believe F11, please post the ARM ARM pseudocode line naming FPSCR for VSEL; otherwise please withdraw it and check the rev-2 tree.

F12 is unchanged and still fixed. Current test line: N2TEST V17 PASS 2264/2264 (ASan+UBSan and -O2).
